hints: Use frequency as the number of wave cycles per second and wavelength as the distance travelled in one cycle.
Multiply the distance per cycle by the number of cycles per second to obtain the distance travelled per second.
walkthrough: In one complete cycle, a wavefront travels one wavelength λ.
A frequency f means that f cycles occur each second.
The distance travelled each second is therefore f × λ.
Speed is distance travelled per unit time, so v = fλ.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses a correct definition of either wavelength as distance per oscillation or frequency as oscillations per unit time.
Combines the definitions with speed as distance per unit time to derive v = fλ.

hints: Read the horizontal distance for one complete cycle on the CRO trace, then use the time-base setting to convert divisions to seconds.
The trace period is four divisions, so calculate T before using f = 1 / T.
walkthrough: One cycle on the trace occupies four horizontal divisions.
With 1.0 ms per division, the period is T = 4 × 1.0 ms = 4.0 × 10⁻³ s.

ai_rubric.observable: Reads four divisions as a period of 4.0 × 10⁻³ s and uses f = 1 / T.
Obtains a detected frequency of 250 Hz.

hints: The source moves towards the stationary observer, so its observed frequency is greater than the source frequency.
Use f_o = f_s v / (v − v_s), with f_o = 250 Hz, f_s = 236 Hz and v_s = 20 m s⁻¹, then rearrange for v.
walkthrough: For a source approaching a stationary observer, use f_o = f_s v / (v − v_s).
Substitute f_o = 250 Hz, f_s = 236 Hz and v_s = 20 m s⁻¹: 250 = 236v / (v − 20).
Hence v = 357 m s⁻¹, which rounds to 360 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the approaching-source Doppler relationship with observed frequency 250 Hz, source frequency 236 Hz and source speed 20 m s⁻¹, then rearranges for sound speed.
Obtains a sound speed of 360 m s⁻¹, allowing a correctly rounded equivalent.
